assessment.nobel_worthiness: Katori's magic-wavelength optical lattice proposal removed Doppler and recoil shifts while retaining many atoms, and Ye's group turned it into clocks at the 10^-18 level. This is a clear, original idea with a transformative measurement outcome, and it underpins tests of fundamental constants, relativistic geodesy and a redefinition of the second. The physics (AC Stark shift cancellation, many-body and atomic-structure control of systematics) is close to core atomic theory.
assessment.attribution: Katori made the decisive conceptual proposal and first demonstrations; Ye's group achieved the leading accuracy and stability and developed the strontium and many-body (Fermi-degenerate) clock platform. A two-person prize is a fair fit to the supplied credit. Other groups (e.g. Lemonde, Sterr and Hollberg in the surrounding clock community) made important contributions that the supplied credit does not include.
assessment.maturity: Independent clocks in several laboratories (strontium, ytterbium) agree and are routinely compared; accuracy has improved steadily over fifteen years. The 2005 prize covered the frequency comb, so this is a clean, timely successor.
uncertainties: Whether ion-clock (Al+) and optical-lattice contributions would be treated as separate topics by the committee.
Whether a redefinition of the SI second, not yet completed, would be seen as a prerequisite for recognition.
I am working from memory of the literature and have not verified priority details independently.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The theoretical prediction of flat bands at a magic twist angle and the 2018 observation of correlated insulating and superconducting states created the field of moire quantum matter, with a tunable platform for correlation physics, fractional Chern insulators and related phenomena. The impact on condensed-matter physics has been rapid and broad.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald made the quantitative 2011 prediction; Jarillo-Herrero's group performed the decisive experiments in 2018. The theory-plus-experiment triplet is a natural configuration, though Cory Dean's group and others have strong claims in the broader moire field and are not in the supplied credit.
assessment.maturity: Many groups reproduced the correlated states and extended them to related systems. The field remains fast-moving, so some interpretations (the nature of the superconductivity) are not settled, but the core discovery is robust.
uncertainties: The pairing mechanism of the superconductivity remains debated.
Whether the committee prefers to wait for more applications or consolidation of the moire field.
Recognition of the closely related contribution on ultrapure hBN substrates, which belongs to a separate candidate.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The observation of a Higgs-like boson in 2012 completed the Standard Model and verified the mechanism recognised by the 2013 prize for theory. This is an experimental discovery of the highest importance, with subsequent measurements of couplings supporting the interpretation.
assessment.attribution: The discovery was made by two very large collaborations, which does not map onto three persons. Gianotti and Virdee led ATLAS and CMS at the time of announcement and Evans led the LHC construction, but Della Negra and Jenni conceived and led the experiments earlier. Any selection involves a difficult and partly arbitrary allocation of credit, and the rules limit a prize to three people.
assessment.maturity: Fully confirmed by two independent experiments and by more than a decade of data. Recognition is not premature, although the 2013 prize reduced the urgency of recognising the experimental side.
uncertainties: The three-person limit versus collaboration credit is unresolved and may keep this candidate from ranking higher.
Whether the committee would consider the experimental discovery sufficiently distinct from the 2013 prize for theory.
Which of Evans, Della Negra, Jenni, Gianotti and Virdee has the strongest claim is a matter of judgement that I cannot resolve from the supplied text.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ultracold atoms in optical lattices realised Hubbard-model physics (superfluid to Mott insulator transition, single-site-resolved microscopy, fermionic quantum gases), turning quantum simulation of correlated matter into a laboratory practice with clean, tunable control. The impact on many-body physics and on quantum simulation platforms is broad and lasting.
assessment.attribution: Zoller (with Jaksch and colleagues) made the theoretical proposal for the Bose-Hubbard model in lattices; Greiner and Bloch performed the Mott insulator and microscope experiments; Esslinger's group made the fermionic Hubbard realisation. The supplied credit gives four people for at most three places, and Jaksch is not in the list, so the allocation is not clean.
assessment.maturity: Highly mature and independently reproduced in many laboratories. The 2001 and 1997 atomic-physics prizes recognised the condensate and cooling, so this is a natural continuation, though quantum simulation of particular hard problems is still developing.
uncertainties: Esslinger is left out of my proposed three, and the choice between Greiner, Bloch and Esslinger is contestable.
Overlap with the neutral-atom quantum computing candidates and with Zoller's separate credit.
Whether simulation has yet delivered a result beyond what classical computation can reach.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit QED reached strong coupling between a superconducting artificial atom and a single microwave photon and became the main architecture for superconducting quantum processors, with dispersive readout, cavity-based coupling and quantum-limited amplification. Its importance for quantum technology and for fundamental tests is substantial and original.
assessment.attribution: The 2004 proposal by Blais, Huang, Wallraff, Girvin and Schoelkopf and the demonstration by Wallraff et al. are the core. The three supplied names are a sensible theory and experiment configuration, but the experimental first demonstration also involved Wallraff, who is not credited here, and the transmon is a separate contribution.
assessment.maturity: Reproduced and extended worldwide. The 2025 prize recognised macroscopic quantum tunnelling in superconducting circuits, so the field has been recently recognised and the committee may regard cQED as a related but distinct discovery that follows naturally.
uncertainties: Possible overlap with the 2025 circuit prize may reduce timeliness.
Uncertain whether the transmon and the cQED architecture would be separated or combined.
Wallraff's role is not in the supplied credit, which limits a fair attribution.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The prediction of the quantum spin Hall state and Z2 topological insulators, followed by observation in HgTe quantum wells, opened a new class of topological phases and shaped a whole research field. The idea is original and conceptually clean, building on topological band-theory ideas related to the 2016 prize.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele made the Z2 prediction; Molenkamp's group made the first experimental observation in HgTe (following the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal, whose authors are not in the supplied credit). The three-person list is a natural fit, but the three-dimensional topological insulator experiments and the BHZ proposal complicate priority.
assessment.maturity: Well established by independent photoemission and transport experiments, and the field has been active for nearly twenty years. Prize recognition is plausible and arguably overdue, though the 2016 prize covered related topology.
uncertainties: BHZ (Bernevig, Hughes, Zhang) and Fu and Kane for 3D materials are not in this credit.
Overlap with the other topological insulator candidate that includes the anomalous Hall effect.
Applications remain limited so far.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantum key distribution (BB84 and the entanglement-based E91 scheme) is an original idea linking fundamental quantum properties to secure communication, and has been commercialised and demonstrated over long distances including by satellite. The concept is clear and has enduring influence on quantum information science.
assessment.attribution: Bennett and Brassard authored BB84; Ekert's 1991 protocol is independent and tied to Bell inequalities. The three-person configuration is natural, and prior art (Wiesner's conjugate coding) is not included in the supplied credit, which is a minor unresolved question.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed by many experiments, though practical security against implementation attacks continues to be studied. The 2022 prize recognised Bell-inequality experiments and quantum information science, so timing is reasonable but there may be partial overlap in the committee's mind.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2022 prize topic.
Whether the committee regards this as primarily computer science or cryptography rather than physics.
Stephen Wiesner's earlier work is not among the credited names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Electromagnetically induced transparency, slow and stopped light, and coherent control of light via atomic coherence are original discoveries in atomic physics with consequences for quantum memories, nonlinear optics and quantum information. The effect is conceptually elegant and widely used.
assessment.attribution: Harris and colleagues demonstrated and developed EIT; Hau's group observed ultraslow light in a Bose-Einstein condensate; Imamoglu contributed to the early theory and subsequent solid-state and photonic extensions. The credit is plausible but not entirely fair, since the earlier coherent population trapping and Fano-interference literature (Arimondo, Alzetta and others) lies behind the effect.
assessment.maturity: Mature and independently confirmed in many systems for over thirty years. Recognition may feel somewhat late but is not premature; the impact on applications is real yet less transformative than the candidates ranked above.
uncertainties: Priority questions related to coherent population trapping and earlier interference work.
Whether the committee sees EIT as a discovery of sufficient breadth compared with the leading candidates.
The specific roles in the theory of EIT versus its experimental demonstration are only partially clear to me from memory.
